senses.definition: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
senses.example: He needs to regain her trust if he is ever going to win her back.

senses.definition: Dependence upon something in the future; hope.
senses.example: Such trust have we through Christ.

senses.definition: Confidence in the future payment for goods or services supplied; credit.
senses.example: I was out of cash, but the landlady let me have it on trust.

senses.definition: That which is committed or entrusted; something received in confidence; a charge.
That upon which confidence is reposed; ground of reliance; hope.
senses.example: O Lord God, thou art my trust from my youth.

senses.definition: Trustworthiness, reliability.
The condition or obligation of one to whom anything is confided; responsible charge or office.
senses.example:
I do profess to be no less than I seem; to serve him truly that
will put me in trust

senses.definition: The confidence vested in a person who has legal ownership of a property to manage for the benefit of another.
senses.example: I put the house into my sister's trust.

senses.definition: An arrangement whereby property or money is given to be held by a third party (a trustee), on the basis that it will be managed for the benefit of, or eventually transferred to, a stated beneficiary; for example, money to be given to a child when he or she reaches adulthood.
A group of businessmen or traders organised for mutual benefit to produce and distribute specific commodities or services, and managed by a central body of trustees.
Affirmation of the access rights of a user of a computer system.
To place confidence in, to rely on, to confide in.
senses.example: We cannot trust anyone who deceives us.
